text:
Tom H: noticing periodic 5-8s p99 latency spikes on prod-rt starting ~16:03 UTC, repeat every ~90s. overall qps steady, but tail jumps. can we triage? :eyes:

infra-bot: alert: p99_latency(prod-rt) > 2s for 3 intervals (16:03-16:08) — alert routed to #eng-runtime

Maya R: saw the alert, pulling traces now. are these correlated to any deploys?

Tom H: no deploys in that window, last deploy 14:12 UTC. rolling deploys were green. attaching a short log excerpt:

```
[16:03:12] request id=abc123 duration=122ms kernel=matmul_q8 batch=12 microbatch=3 kv_cache=hit
[16:03:13] request id=def456 duration=2110ms kernel=fallback_gemm batch=8 microbatch=1 kv_cache=miss
[16:03:13] request id=ghi789 duration=1870ms kernel=fallback_gemm batch=7 microbatch=1 kv_cache=miss
[16:03:14] request id=jkl012 duration=130ms kernel=matmul_q8 batch=13 microbatch=4 kv_cache=hit
```

Ben K: interesting — kernel flips to fallback_gemm when batch size drops below ~9, and those requests show kv_cache misses. I'm seeing kernel selector metric oscillating 12 -> 8 -> 12 repeatedly in the timeline. pulling a flamegraph + selector trace now. link: https://internal.fg/redwood/2248123456 (flamegraph)

Li W: hypothesis: admission control is stepping aggressively when a small burst drains the continuous batcher, causing microbatch admission to oscillate. when the batcher rebuilds it picks the fast kernel (matmul_q8), but the small shards immediately evict parts of the KV cache leading to misses and fallback kernels. resonance between admission steps and kv-eviction.

Maya R: that matches the traces i see — KV cache hit rate for that shard drops from 92% -> 18% during the spike window. I exported a quick perf sample:

```
# perf top (sample)
  18.4%  runtime_binary  kernel_fallback_gemm
  12.1%  runtime_binary  kv_cache_lookup
   9.8%  libm.so        matmul_q8
```

Ben K: also saw an admission metric histogram with step boundaries at {0.2, 0.5, 0.8} load — the controller uses deterministic thresholds (no jitter). when load crosses 0.5 we drop the admission score and a bunch of microbatches get admitted almost in lockstep. that creates the 'burst wave' and transiently small batches.

Tom H: repro idea: run a synthetic load that pulses 1.5x for 10s every 90s and collect kernel_selector, kv_hit, microbatch_size over time. anyone has a quick runner?

Ben K: i can run it in staging. quick patch i want to test: add 200-500ms randomized jitter to admission window and bump kv_cache.reserved_ratio by 10% to reduce eviction sensitivity. CLI patch: `redwoodctl apply --set admission.jitter=0.3s --set kv_cache.reserved_ratio=0.60`

Li W: long term we should: (1) add hysteresis to the admission controller so it only steps after sustained crossing, (2) make kernel selector prefer stability (avoid flipping kernels inside a 2s window unless benefit > X), (3) add microbatch age as a factor to kernel choice so older microbatches don't force small-kernel fallbacks.

Maya R: agree. also adding small randomized delay to microbatch flushes (10-50ms) might de-synchronize drains without raising latency much.

oncall-sre: rolled back the batching heuristic change from 15:58 (PR #3421) as a quick mitigation — preliminary dashboards show p99 from ~2.3s -> ~320ms over the last 6 minutes. keeping an eye. :thumbsup:

Tom H: good catch on rollback, thanks. Ben — can you run the staged pulse with the jitter + reserved_ratio tweak and post graphs? prioritize KV hit rate and kernel_selector flip count.

Ben K: running now in staging (job id: perf-pulse-224812). expecting results in ~12m. will post snapshots.

Maya R: filing a follow-up issue with proposed fixes and experiments: GH #4678. assigning to Li (owner), Ben (experiment), Tom (prod rollback/coord).

Li W: i'll prototype admission hysteresis next week. idea: require two consecutive intervals > threshold and add exponential backoff on step-down. also i'll add a metric for 'resonant_flip_count' to quantify the oscillation.

Tom H: cool. action items:
- (Ben) post staging pulse graphs + KV hit timeline + kernel flip counts (due in 12m)
- (Li) prototype hysteresis + resonant_flip_count metric (due EOW)
- (Maya) capture traces for any future spikes and attach flamegraphs (ongoing)
- (oncall-sre) keep prod rollback until mitigations validated

Ben K: posted initial graphs: KV hit dip now reduced to 65% with jitter + reserved_ratio tweak, kernel flips down 70%. p99 in staging stayed below 350ms. link: https://internal.metrics/staging/224812/pulse (graphs)

Tom H: thanks — marking this thread triaged. we'll keep monitoring and aim for a canary deploy of admission hysteresis once Li's prototype is up. :white_check_mark:
